page_title: AutoDoc | Open-source AI meeting notes for Mac and Windows

summary.name: AutoDoc
summary.one_liner: AutoDoc is an open-source meeting notes app for Mac and Windows that records screen, mic and system audio, and creates editable notes with local AI processing.
use_cases: Keeping confidential legal, healthcare, finance or HR meetings off vendor servers
Reviewing editable meeting notes and replaying key moments from timestamps
Searching past meeting transcripts and notes
Asking questions across meeting history with local AI
Recording client calls with a searchable local archive
Transcribing meetings in one of 27 supported languages
summary.what_it_does: AutoDoc detects an active meeting and asks before recording. It captures screen video, microphone, and system audio from the device, without a meeting bot. Transcription, notes, and Ask AI run locally, and the transcript and notes stay linked to the recording so an available timestamp can be replayed. Notes can be edited and exported as PDF, Word, or Markdown, and transcripts and notes are searchable. Microphone audio is labeled "Me" and combined system audio is labeled "Them", without identifying individual remote participants.
notable: Local AI processing with no cloud AI service or AI API key needed
Screen video captured alongside audio for timestamped replay
Supports 27 meeting languages on sufficiently powerful hardware
Open source under AGPL-3.0, built by the team behind Duet Display
caveats: 8 GB Macs and lower-spec Windows PCs are English-only and use a smaller notes model with slower processing after meetings
Local AI setup needs roughly 10 GB of disk space plus space for recordings
Ask AI answers should be reviewed before relying on them
